s1.syndrome_frame: Altered mental status with focal neurological deficits and fever, progressing to obtundation
salient_findings: Left upper- and lower-limb weakness
Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on noncontrast head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema on brain MRI
CSF with elevated WBCs, protein, and decreased glucose
Progression of neurological deficits and imaging findings despite empirical antibiotic treatment
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5) without meningeal signs
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT showed hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage
Brain MRI showed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema
CSF with 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL
Empirical IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir were begun
Leukocytosis improved but fever persisted
Repeat lumbar puncture showed increased WBCs, protein, and decreased glucose
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits, fever, and imaging findings of a hypodense area with mass effect are consistent with a brain abscess

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use increase the risk of opportunistic infections like toxoplasmosis, which can cause focal neurological deficits and altered mental status

shortlist.label: Cerebral Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Altered mental status, fever, and focal neurological deficits can be seen in cerebral tuberculosis, especially in the context of a compromised immune system

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use increases the risk of opportunistic infections like PML, which can cause progressive neurological decline

shortlist.label: Cerebral Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits, altered mental status, and imaging findings of a hypodense area with mass effect are consistent with cerebral cryptococcosis, an opportunistic infection that can occur in immunocompromised individuals

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with altered mental status, fever, and focal neurological deficits, along with imaging findings of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect and subsequent progression on repeat MRI, is most consistent with a brain abscess. The presence of leukocytosis, elevated CSF protein, and decreased CSF glucose also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While possible in an immunocompromised patient, the lack of specific evidence for toxoplasmosis and the presence of mass effect on imaging make brain abscess more likely

rejected.label: Cerebral Tuberculosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not strongly suggest tuberculosis, and the CSF findings are not typical for tuberculous meningitis

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: This diagnosis typically presents with a more subacute course and lacks the mass effect and significant CSF pleocytosis seen in this patient

rejected.label: Cerebral Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: While possible in an immunocompromised patient, the lack of specific evidence for cryptococcosis and the presence of mass effect on imaging make brain abscess more likely
